He was crucified also for us, suffered under Pontius Pilate, and was buried. And the third day He rose again according to the Scriptures. L.7e0: May the performance of my homage be pleasing to Thee, O holy Trinity: and grant that the Sacrifice which I, though unworthy, have offered up in the sight of Thy Majesty, may be acceptable to Thee, and through Thy mercy, be a propitiation for me, and for all those for whom I have offered it. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

L.nbz: In princípio erat Verbum, et Verbum erat apud Deum, et Deus erat Verbum. Hoc erat in princípio apud Deum. Omnia per ipsum facta sunt: et sine ipso factum est nihil, quod factum est: in ipso vita erat, et vita erat lux hóminum: et lux in ténebris lucet, et ténebræ eam non comprehendérunt.
L.mir: Fuit homo missus a Deo, cui nomen erat Ioánnes. Hic venit in testimónium, ut testimónium perhibéret de lúmine, ut omnes créderent per illum. Non erat ille lux, sed ut testimónium perhibéret de lúmine.
L.m3d: Erat lux vera, quæ illúminat omnem hóminem veniéntem in hunc mundum. In mundo erat, et mundus per ipsum factus est, et mundus eum non cognóvit. In própria venit, et sui eum non recepérunt. Quotquot autem recepérunt eum, dedit eis potestátem fílios Dei fíeri, his, qui credunt in nómine eius: qui non ex sanguínibus, neque ex voluntáte carnis, neque ex voluntáte viri, sed ex Deo nati sunt. ^Genuflectit dicens:^ Et Verbum caro factum est, ^Et surgens prosequitur:^ et habitávit in nobis: et vídimus glóriam eius, glóriam quasi Unigéniti a Patre, plenum grátiæ et veritátis.
L.12kq: ^Finito Evangelio sancti Ioannis, discedens ab Altari, pro gratiarum actione dicit Ant. Trium puerórum, cum reliquis, ut habetur in principio Missalis.^

L.qrf: The beginning ^+^ of the holy Gospel according to John
L.nda: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. The same was in the beginning with God. All things were made by Him, and without Him was made nothing that was made: in Him was life, and the life was the Light of men; and the Light shineth in darkness, and the darkness did not comprehend it. There was a man sent from God, whose name was John. This man came for a witness, to testify concerning the Light, that all might believe through Him. He was not the Light, but he was to testify concerning the Light. That was the true Light, which enlighteneth every man that cometh into this world. He was in the world, and the world was made by Him, and the world knew Him not. He came unto His own, and His own received Him not. But as many as received Him to them He gave power to become sons of God, to them that believe in His Name, who are born not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God. ^Here all kneel.^ And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us: and we saw His glory, the glory as of the Only begotten of the Father, full of grace and truth.
L.13sl: ^S.^ Ave María, grátia plena, Dóminus tecum, benedícta tu in muliéribus et benedíctus fructus ventris tui, Iesus.
L.137u: ^O.^ Sancta María, Mater Dei, ora pro nobis peccatóribus, nunc et in hora mortis nostræ. Amen.
L.137t: ^O.^ Salve Regína, Mater misericórdiæ, vita, dulcédo, et spes nostra, salve. Ad te clamámus, éxsules fílii Evæ. Ad te suspirámus geméntes et flentes in hac lacrymárum valle. Eia ergo, Advocáta nostra, illos tuos misericórdes óculos ad nos convérte. Et Iesum, benedíctum fructum ventris tui, nobis, post hoc exílium, osténde. O clemens, o pia, o dulcis Virgo Mária.
L.13sx: ^S.^ Ora pro nobis, sancta Dei Génitrix.
L.13sy: ^S.^ Orémus. Deus, refúgium nostrum et virtus, pópulum ad te clamántem propítius réspice; et intercedénte gloriósa, et immaculáta Vírgine Dei Genitríce María, cum beáto Ioseph, eius Sponso, ac beatis Apóstolis tuis Petro et Paulo, et ómnibus Sanctis, quas pro conversióne peccatórum, pro libertáte et exaltatióne sanctæ Matris Ecclésiæ, preces effúndimus, miséricors et benígnus exáudi. Per eúndem Christum Dóminum nostrum. Amen.
L.137v: ^O.^ Sancte Míchaël Archángele, defénde nos in prǽlio; contra nequítiam et insídias diáboli esto præsídium. Imperet illi Deus, súpplices deprecámur: tuque, Princeps milítiæ Cæléstis, sátanam aliósque spíritus malígnos, qui ad perditiónem animárum pervagántur in mundo, divína virtúte in inférnum detrúde. Amen.
L.13xz: ^To be said kneeling after the celebration of Low Mass.^
L.138s: ^P.^ Hail Mary, full of grace; The Lord is with thee; Blessed art thou amongst women, And blessed is the fruit of thy womb, Jesus.
L.y4h: ^A.^ Holy Mary, Mother of God, Pray for us sinners, now and at the hour of our death. Amen.
L.y4f: ^A.^ Hail, holy Queen, Mother of Mercy, our life, our sweetness, and our hope. To thee do we cry, poor banished children of Eve. To thee do we send up our sighs, mourning and weeping in this valley of tears. Turn then, most gracious Advocate, thine eyes of mercy towards us. And after this our exile, show unto us the blessed Fruit of thy womb, Jesus. O clement, O loving, O sweet Virgin Mary.
L.1393: ^P.^ Pray for us, O Holy Mother of God.
L.137w: ^O.^ That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.
L.138v: ^P.^ Let us pray. O God, our refuge and our strength, look down in mercy on Thy people who cry to Thee; and by the intercession of the glorious and Immaculate Virgin Mary, Mother of God, of St. Joseph her Spouse, of Thy blessed Apostles Peter and Paul, and of all the Saints, in mercy and goodness hear our prayers for the conversion of sinners, and for the liberty and exaltation of our holy Mother the Church. Through the same Christ our Lord. Amen.
L.y4i: ^A.^ Holy Michael Archangel, defend us in the day of battle; be our safeguard against the wickedness and snares of the devil. -- May God rebuke him, we humbly pray: and do thou, Prince of the heavenly host, by the power of God thrust down to hell Satan and all wicked spirits, who wander through the world for the ruin of souls. Amen.
L.11br: ^Ant.^ The Lord, the King of Confessors, * O come, let us worship.
L.81o: ^34:1^ Iúdica, Dómine, nocéntes me, * expúgna impugnántes me.
L.82a: ^34:2^ Apprehénde arma et scutum: * et exsúrge in adiutórium mihi.
L.82d: ^34:3^ Effúnde frámeam, et conclúde advérsus eos, qui persequúntur me: * dic ánimæ meæ: Salus tua ego sum.
L.82f: ^34:4^ Confundántur et revereántur, * quæréntes ánimam meam.
L.82e: ^34:4^ Avertántur retrórsum, et confundántur * cogitántes mihi mala.
L.82i: ^34:5^ Fiant tamquam pulvis ante fáciem venti: * et Ángelus Dómini coárctans eos.
L.82k: ^34:6^ Fiat via illórum ténebræ et lúbricum: * et Ángelus Dómini pérsequens eos.
L.82n: ^34:7^ Quóniam gratis abscondérunt mihi intéritum láquei sui: * supervácue exprobravérunt ánimam meam.
L.82p: ^34:8^ Véniat illi láqueus, quem ignórat: et cáptio, quam abscóndit, apprehéndat eum: * et in láqueum cadat in ipsum.
L.82r: ^34:9^ Ánima autem mea exsultábit in Dómino: * et delectábitur super salutári suo.
L.813: ^34:10^ Ómnia ossa mea dicent: * Dómine, quis símilis tibi?
L.811: ^34:10^ Erípiens ínopem de manu fortiórum eius: * egénum et páuperem a diripiéntibus eum.
L.10od: ^Ant.^ Overthrow, O Lord, * them that fight against me.
L.81p: ^34:1^ Judge thou, O Lord, them that wrong me: * overthrow them that fight against me.
L.82b: ^34:2^ Take hold of arms and shield: * and rise up to help me.
L.82c: ^34:3^ Bring out the sword, and shut up the way against them that persecute me: * say to my soul: I am thy salvation.
L.82g: ^34:4^ Let them be confounded and ashamed * that seek after my soul.
L.82h: ^34:4^ Let them be turned back and be confounded * that devise against me.
L.82j: ^34:5^ Let them become as dust before the wind: * and let the Angel of the Lord straiten them.
L.82l: ^34:6^ Let their way become dark and slippery; * and let the Angel of the Lord pursue them.
L.82m: ^34:7^ For without cause they have hidden their net for me unto destruction: * without cause they have upbraided my soul.
L.82o: ^34:8^ Let the snare which he knoweth not come upon him: and let the net which he hath hidden catch him: * and into that very snare let them fall.
L.82q: ^34:9^ But my soul shall rejoice in the Lord; * and shall be delighted in his salvation.
L.810: ^34:10^ All my bones shall say: * Lord, who is like to thee?
L.812: ^34:10^ Who deliverest the poor from the hand of them that are stronger than he; * the needy and the poor from them that strip him.
L.10oe: ^Ant.^ Overthrow, O Lord, them that fight against me.
L.10wk: ^Ant.^ Restítue ánimam meam * a malefáctis eórum, Dómine.
L.814: ^34:11^ Surgéntes testes iníqui, * quæ ignorábam interrogábant me.
L.816: ^34:12^ Retribuébant mihi mala pro bonis: * sterilitátem ánimæ meæ.
L.819: ^34:13^ Ego autem cum mihi molésti essent, * induébar cilício.
L.81a: ^34:13^ Humiliábam in ieiúnio ánimam meam: * et orátio mea in sinu meo convertétur.
L.81d: ^34:14^ Quasi próximum, et quasi fratrem nostrum, sic complacébam: * quasi lugens et contristátus, sic humiliábar.
L.81f: ^34:15^ Et advérsum me lætáti sunt, et convenérunt: * congregáta sunt super me flagélla, et ignorávi.
L.81g: ^34:16^ Dissipáti sunt, nec compúncti, tentavérunt me, subsannavérunt me subsannatióne: * frenduérunt super me déntibus suis.
L.81i: ^34:17^ Dómine, quando respícies? * restítue ánimam meam a malignitáte eórum, a leónibus únicam meam.
L.10wl: ^Ant.^ Restítue ánimam meam a malefáctis eórum, Dómine.
L.10w8: ^Ant.^ Rescue, O Lord, * my soul from their malice.
L.815: ^34:11^ Unjust witnesses rising up * have asked me things I knew not.
L.817: ^34:12^ They repaid me evil for good: * to the depriving me of my soul.
L.818: ^34:13^ But as for me, when they were troublesome to me, * I was clothed with haircloth.
L.81b: ^34:13^ I humbled my soul with fasting; * and my prayer shall be turned into my bosom.
L.81c: ^34:14^ As a neighbour and as an own brother, so did I please: * as one mourning and sorrowful so was I humbled.
L.81e: ^34:15^ But they rejoiced against me, and came together: * scourges were gathered together upon me, and I knew not.
L.81h: ^34:16^ They were separated, and repented not: they tempted me, they scoffed at me with scorn: * they gnashed upon me with their teeth.
L.81j: ^34:17^ Lord, when wilt thou look upon me? * rescue thou my soul from their malice: my only one from the lions.
L.10w9: ^Ant.^ Rescue, O Lord, my soul from their malice.
L.zb9: ^Ant.^ Exsúrge, Dómine, * et inténde iudício meo.
L.81k: ^34:18^ Confitébor tibi in ecclésia magna, * in pópulo gravi laudábo te.
L.81n: ^34:19^ Non supergáudeant mihi qui adversántur mihi iníque: * qui odérunt me gratis et ánnuunt óculis.
L.81r: ^34:20^ Quóniam mihi quidem pacífice loquebántur: * et in iracúndia terræ loquéntes, dolos cogitábant.
L.81t: ^34:21^ Et dilatavérunt super me os suum: * dixérunt: Euge, euge, vidérunt óculi nostri.
L.81v: ^34:22^ Vidísti, Dómine, ne síleas: * Dómine, ne discédas a me.
L.81x: ^34:23^ Exsúrge et inténde iudício meo: * Deus meus, et Dóminus meus in causam meam.
L.81y: ^34:24^ Iúdica me secúndum iustítiam tuam, Dómine, Deus meus, * et non supergáudeant mihi.
L.821: ^34:25^ Non dicant in córdibus suis: Euge, euge, ánimæ nostræ: * nec dicant: Devorávimus eum.
L.822: ^34:26^ Erubéscant et revereántur simul, * qui gratulántur malis meis.
L.823: ^34:26^ Induántur confusióne et reveréntia * qui magna loquúntur super me.
L.826: ^34:27^ Exsúltent et læténtur qui volunt iustítiam meam: * et dicant semper: Magnificétur Dóminus qui volunt pacem servi eius.
L.829: ^34:28^ Et lingua mea meditábitur iustítiam tuam, * tota die laudem tuam.
L.zbb: ^Ant.^ Exsúrge, Dómine, et inténde iudício meo.
L.yi9: ^Ant.^ Arise, O Lord, * and be attentive to my judgment.
L.81l: ^34:18^ I will give thanks to thee in a great church; * I will praise thee in a strong people.
L.81m: ^34:19^ Let not them that are my enemies wrongfully rejoice over me: * who have hated me without cause, and wink with the eyes.
L.81q: ^34:20^ For they spoke indeed peaceably to me; * and speaking in the anger of the earth they devised guile.
L.81s: ^34:21^ And they opened their mouth wide against me; * they said: Well done, well done, our eyes have seen it.
L.81u: ^34:22^ Thou hast seen, O Lord, be not thou silent: * O Lord, depart not from me.
L.81w: ^34:23^ Arise, and be attentive to my judgment: * to my cause, my God, and my Lord.
L.81z: ^34:24^ Judge me, O Lord my God according to thy justice, * and let them not rejoice over me.
L.820: ^34:25^ Let them not say in their hearts: It is well, it is well, to our mind: * neither let them say: We have swallowed him up.
L.825: ^34:26^ Let them blush: and be ashamed together, * who rejoice at my evils.
L.824: ^34:26^ Let them be clothed with confusion and shame, * who speak great things against me.
L.827: ^34:27^ Let them rejoice and be glad, who are well pleased with my justice, * and let them say always: The Lord be magnified, who delights in the peace of his servant.
L.828: ^34:28^ And my tongue shall meditate thy justice, * thy praise all the day long.
L.yib: ^Ant.^ Arise, O Lord, and be attentive to my judgment.
L.10c5: ^Ant.^ Noli æmulári * in eo qui prosperátur et facit iniquitátem.
L.83f: ^36:1^ Noli æmulári in malignántibus: * neque zeláveris faciéntes iniquitátem.
L.843: ^36:2^ Quóniam tamquam fænum velóciter aréscent: * et quemádmodum ólera herbárum cito décident.
L.84o: ^36:3^ Spera in Dómino, et fac bonitátem: * et inhábita terram, et pascéris in divítiis eius.
L.84s: ^36:4^ Delectáre in Dómino: * et dabit tibi petitiónes cordis tui.
L.84v: ^36:5^ Revéla Dómino viam tuam, et spera in eo: * et ipse fáciet.
L.84x: ^36:6^ Et edúcet quasi lumen iustítiam tuam: et iudícium tuum tamquam merídiem: * súbditus esto Dómino, et ora eum.
L.84z: ^36:7^ Noli æmulári in eo, qui prosperátur in via sua: * in hómine faciénte iniustítias.
L.851: ^36:8^ Désine ab ira, et derelínque furórem: * noli æmulári ut malignéris.
L.853: ^36:9^ Quóniam qui malignántur, exterminabúntur: * sustinéntes autem Dóminum, ipsi hereditábunt terram.
L.82s: ^36:10^ Et adhuc pusíllum, et non erit peccátor: * et quæres locum eius et non invénies.
L.82v: ^36:11^ Mansuéti autem hereditábunt terram: * et delectabúntur in multitúdine pacis.
L.82w: ^36:12^ Observábit peccátor iustum: * et stridébit super eum déntibus suis.
L.82z: ^36:13^ Dóminus autem irridébit eum: * quóniam próspicit quod véniet dies eius.
L.830: ^36:14^ Gládium evaginavérunt peccatóres: * intendérunt arcum suum,
L.833: ^36:14^ Ut deíciant páuperem et ínopem: * ut trucídent rectos corde.
L.834: ^36:15^ Gládius eórum intret in corda ipsórum: * et arcus eórum confringátur.
L.10c6: ^Ant.^ Noli æmulári in eo qui prosperátur et facit iniquitátem.
L.z80: ^Ant.^ Envy not * the man who prospereth in his way; the man who doth unjust things.
L.83e: ^36:1^ Be not emulous of evildoers; * nor envy them that work iniquity.
L.842: ^36:2^ For they shall shortly wither away as grass, * and as the green herbs shall quickly fall.
L.84p: ^36:3^ Trust in the Lord, and do good, * and dwell in the land, and thou shalt be fed with its riches.
L.84t: ^36:4^ Delight in the Lord, * and he will give thee the requests of thy heart.
L.84u: ^36:5^ Commit thy way to the Lord, and trust in him, * and he will do it.
L.84w: ^36:6^ And he will bring forth thy justice as the light, and thy judgment as the noonday: * be subject to the Lord and pray to him.
L.84y: ^36:7^ Envy not the man who prospereth in his way; * the man who doth unjust things.
L.850: ^36:8^ Cease from anger, and leave rage; * have no emulation to do evil.
L.852: ^36:9^ For the evildoers shall be cut off: * but they that wait upon the Lord shall inherit the land.
L.82t: ^36:10^ For yet a little while, and the wicked shall not be: * and thou shalt seek his place, and shalt not find it.
L.82u: ^36:11^ But the meek shall inherit the land, * and shall delight in abundance of peace.
L.82x: ^36:12^ The sinner shall watch the just man: * and shall gnash upon him with his teeth.
L.82y: ^36:13^ But the Lord shall laugh at him: * for he foreseeth that his day shall come.
L.831: ^36:14^ The wicked have drawn out the sword: * they have bent their bow.
L.832: ^36:14^ To cast down the poor and needy, * to kill the upright of heart.
L.835: ^36:15^ Let their sword enter into their own hearts, * and let their bow be broken.
L.z81: ^Ant.^ Envy not the man who prospereth in his way; the man who doth unjust things.
L.yqr: ^Ant.^ Brácchia peccatórum * conteréntur, confírmat autem iustos Dóminus.
L.837: ^36:16^ Mélius est módicum iusto, * super divítias peccatórum multas.
L.839: ^36:17^ Quóniam brácchia peccatórum conteréntur: * confírmat autem iustos Dóminus.
L.83a: ^36:18^ Novit Dóminus dies immaculatórum: * et heréditas eórum in ætérnum erit.
L.83c: ^36:19^ Non confundéntur in témpore malo, et in diébus famis saturabúntur: * quia peccatóres períbunt.
L.83h: ^36:20^ Inimíci vero Dómini mox ut honorificáti fúerint et exaltáti: * deficiéntes, quemádmodum fumus defícient.
L.83i: ^36:21^ Mutuábitur peccátor, et non solvet: * iustus autem miserétur et tríbuet.
L.83l: ^36:22^ Quia benedicéntes ei hereditábunt terram: * maledicéntes autem ei disperíbunt.
L.83m: ^36:23^ Apud Dóminum gressus hóminis dirigéntur: * et viam eius volet.
L.83o: ^36:24^ Cum cecíderit non collidétur: * quia Dóminus suppónit manum suam.
L.83r: ^36:25^ Iúnior fui, étenim sénui: * et non vidi iustum derelíctum, nec semen eius quærens panem.
L.83t: ^36:26^ Tota die miserétur et cómmodat: * et semen illíus in benedictióne erit.
L.83v: ^36:27^ Declína a malo, et fac bonum: * et inhábita in sǽculum sǽculi.
L.83y: ^36:28^ Quia Dóminus amat iudícium, et non derelínquet sanctos suos: * in ætérnum conservabúntur.
L.83x: ^36:28^ Iniústi puniéntur: * et semen impiórum períbit.
L.841: ^36:29^ Iusti autem hereditábunt terram: * et inhabitábunt in sǽculum sǽculi super eam.
L.yqs: ^Ant.^ Brácchia peccatórum conteréntur, confírmat autem iustos Dóminus.
L.11cw: ^Ant.^ The arms of the wicked * shall be broken in pieces; but the Lord strengtheneth the just.
L.836: ^36:16^ Better is a little to the just, * than the great riches of the wicked.
L.838: ^36:17^ For the arms of the wicked shall be broken in pieces; * but the Lord strengtheneth the just.
L.83b: ^36:18^ The Lord knoweth the days of the undefiled; * and their inheritance shall be for ever.
L.83d: ^36:19^ They shall not be confounded in the evil time; and in the days of famine they shall be filled, * because the wicked shall perish.

Quinque autem ex eis erant fátuæ, et quinque prudéntes: sed quinque fátuæ, accéptis lampádibus, non sumpsérunt óleum secum: prudéntes vero accepérunt óleum in vasis suis cum lampádibus. Moram autem faciénte sponso, dormitavérunt omnes et dormiérunt. Média autem nocte clamor factus est: Ecce, sponsus venit, exíte óbviam ei. Tunc surrexérunt omnes vírgines íllæ, et ornavérunt lámpades suas. Fátuæ autem sapiéntibus dixérunt: Date nobis de óleo vestro: quia lámpades nostræ exstinguúntur. Respondérunt prudéntes, dicéntes: Ne forte non suffíciat nobis et vobis, ite pótius ad vendéntes, et émite vobis. Dum autem irent émere, venit sponsus: et quæ parátæ erant, intravérunt cum eo ad núptias, et clausa est iánua. Novíssime vero véniunt et réliquæ vírgines, dicéntes: Dómine, Dómine, áperi nobis. At ille respóndens, ait: Amen, dico vobis, néscio vos. Vigiláte ítaque, quia nescítis diem neque horam.
L.krl: At that time Jesus spoke this parable to His disciples: “Then will the kingdom of heaven be like ten virgins who took their lamps and went forth to meet the bridegroom and the bride. Five of them were foolish and five wise. But the five foolish, when they took their lamps, took no oil with them, while the wise did take oil in their vessels with the lamps. Then as the bridegroom was long in coming, they all became drowsy and slept. And at midnight a cry arose, 'Behold, the bridegroom is coming, go forth to meet him!' Then all those virgins arose and trimmed their lamps. And the foolish said to the wise, 'Give us some of your oil, for our lamps are going out.' The wise answered, saying, 'Lest there may not be enough for us and for you, go rather to those who sell it, and buy some for yourselves.' Now while they were gone to buy it, the bridegroom came; and those who were ready went in with him to the marriage feast, and the door was shut. Finally there came also the other virgins, who said, 'Sir, sir, open the door for us!' But he answered and said, 'Amen I say to you, I do not know you.' Watch therefore, for you know neither the day nor the hour.”
